Ephraimites
EE-fray-um-ites
n. pl.
The descendants of Ephraim, Joseph’s younger son, whom Jacob deliberately blessed above Manasseh with crossed hands. Their name means doubly fruitful, and their tribe became so dominant in the north that the prophets use Ephraim as the standing name for the whole northern kingdom.

Biblical Definition

The Ephraimites are the leading tribe of the north, and Scripture’s portrait of them is of great gifts joined to a chronic quarrelsomeness. Jacob crossed his hands over Joseph’s sons and gave the greater blessing to the younger: truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations (Genesis 48:19). Joshua was an Ephraimite, and the tabernacle stood in their territory at Shiloh for centuries. But they failed the first test of the conquest — they drave not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer: but the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites unto this day (Joshua 16:10) — and they spent the era of the judges complaining of being left out of other men’s battles. They chid with Gideon sharply for not calling them (Judges 8:1); they threatened to burn Jephthah’s house over his head, and at the passages of Jordan their own dialect betrayed them: Say now Shibboleth: and he said Sibboleth… and there fell at that time of the Ephraimites forty and two thousand (Judges 12:6). Jeroboam was an Ephrathite of Zereda, and after him Ephraim is Hosea’s and Isaiah’s name for the apostate northern kingdom — Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned (Hosea 7:8). Isaiah promises the healing of the ancient quarrel: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 has no EPHRAIMITE entry. The Hebrew Ephrayim is a dual form meaning double fruitfulness, explained at Genesis 41:52: God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

expand to see more

EPHRAIMITE, n. — A descendant of Ephraim, the younger son of Joseph; a member of the chief tribe of the northern kingdom.

Genesis 41:52 supplies the naming: Joseph called the second son Ephraim, For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

Mount Ephraim, the central highland, held Shiloh, Shechem, Bethel, and Timnathserah where Joshua was buried.

In Hosea, Isaiah, and Jeremiah, Ephraim commonly denotes the whole northern kingdom of the ten tribes.

The word Shibboleth, an ear of corn or a flowing stream, entered English from Judges 12:6 as the name for any test-word that betrays an outsider.

Key Scripture

Genesis 48:19 — "And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations."

Joshua 16:10 — "And they drave not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer: but the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites unto this day, and serve under tribute."

Judges 8:1 — "And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply."

Judges 12:6 — "Then said they unto him, Say now Shibboleth: and he said Sibboleth: for he could not frame to pronounce it right. Then they took him, and slew him at the passages of Jordan: and there fell at that time of the Ephraimites forty and two thousand."

Hosea 7:8 — "Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned."

Modern Corruption

Hosea’s image of a cake not turned — burnt on one side, raw on the other — is the sharpest description in Scripture of the half-converted religion that is now the default in the English-speaking church.

expand to see more

A cake not turned is scorched where it faced the fire and uncooked where it did not. Hosea means an Ephraim zealous in one department of religion and untouched in another: keeping the feasts and keeping the calves, courting Egypt and courting Assyria, energetic and useless. The condition is not hypocrisy, which knows itself; the next verse says gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not. The modern equivalents are easy to name and unpleasant to hear — passionate about doctrine and cold at home, generous in public and dishonest in business, orthodox on paper and prayerless. The remedy Hosea preaches is not more heat on the same side. It is repentance, which is being turned.

The Ephraimite temper is the second thing worth naming, because churches reproduce it constantly. Twice the tribe arrives after a battle it did not fight to complain of not being invited, and the second time it costs forty-two thousand lives at the fords. Gideon answered them softly and turned away wrath; Jephthah answered them in kind and the river ran with their dead. Proverbs was not yet written, but the two chapters together are a commentary on it. A man’s wounded standing is one of the most destructive forces in the life of a congregation, and the reason it does so much damage is that it always presents itself as a concern for the work.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Ephrayim (H669), double fruitfulness, from parah to be fruitful; the gentilic Ephrathi (H673) serves both for Ephraimite and for Ephrathite of Bethlehem.

expand to see more

Hebrew Ephrayim (H669) — Ephraim; a dual form, double fruitfulness (Genesis 41:52).

Hebrew parah (H6509) — to bear fruit, to be fruitful; the root of the name.

Hebrew Ephrathi (H673) — Ephraimite, and also Ephrathite; context distinguishes the tribe from the men of Bethlehem Ephratah.

Hebrew shibboleth (H7641) — an ear of corn, or a flowing stream; the test-word of Judges 12:6.

Hebrew ugah beli hafukah — a cake not turned (Hosea 7:8), a flat loaf burnt on one side and raw on the other.

Usage

"The Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites unto this day (Joshua 16:10) — the conquest left unfinished in the strongest tribe."

"Say now Shibboleth: and he said Sibboleth (Judges 12:6) — the syllable that cost forty-two thousand men."

"Ephraim is a cake not turned (Hosea 7:8) — half-baked religion named by a prophet."
